display_information.description: An AI agent in a session its owner watches. While it listens, people on its roster tag it; it investigates, answers with evidence, acts.
display_information.long_description: TIER — STANDARD + AGENTS (opt-in, on top of the default). ENABLES: everything STANDARD does, plus Slack's Agents feature and the `assistant:write` scope it carries. RISK: STANDARD's permissions, plus one cost that cannot be undone — enabling the Agents feature is IRREVERSIBLE, workspace guests lose access to the app, and it needs a reinstall. Answering a tag does not use it, so take STANDARD unless you specifically want thread titles or suggested prompts. FIELDS TO POPULATE before pasting: {{APP_NAME}} and {{BOT_DISPLAY_NAME}} — set them to what you want this app and its bot called in Slack. FIRST INSTALL ONLY. A Slack manifest is applied whole: pasting this over an app that already exists renames it and its bot, and revokes every scope this file does not list. To change a live app, export its own manifest from api.slack.com/apps and edit that instead.
display_information.name: {{APP_NAME}}

agent_view.agent_description: An AI agent running in a Claude Code session its owner can watch. While it is listening, tag it in a thread or a DM: it investigates with live tools and the team's own history, replies with the evidence, and can raise the pull request or file the ticket. It answers only a short roster of people unless its owner opens it to everyone.
